title: How do we write each repeated multiplication as a power?
description: Six repeated multiplications of numbers and letters are written with exponents by counting how often each factor repeats. The counts are then checked against the factors on the board.
teaching_notes: One idea: count how many times each factor repeats and write that count as its exponent. Watch for students who write the count of all the factors instead of the count of each factor.

video_script.why: The child can write four sixes multiplied as a power and now does it for six repeated multiplications, with one factor or several.
video_script.substitution: Six new repeated multiplications of numbers and letters, each counted factor by factor.
video_script.anchor: the six repeated multiplications on the board, each with its repeated factors circled
video_script.payoff_line: The last one is eigh cubed, see to the power four, dee

final_answer.spoken: six to the power four; why squared; bee to the power four; five squared times seven cubed; two squared times eigh squared; and eigh cubed, see to the power four, dee

maths_rules: a × a × a × c × c × c × c × d = a³c⁴d (d once, no exponent)
video_script.design: One idea: count each repeated factor and write the count as its exponent. The six multiplications stay on the board all video; the check compares the counts with the factors written.

narration: <bookmark mark='cube'/>Two times two times two is two to the power three.
<bookmark mark='count'/>The small number counts how many times two is multiplied.

marks.one: the repeats in each of the first three are counted
marks.third: y × y = y² and b × b × b × b = b⁴ are written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, count the repeats, the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Six repeats four times, so the first is six to the power four.
The letter why repeats twice, so it is why squared.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Bee repeats four times, so the third is bee to the power four.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, the fourth has five twice and seven three times.
It is five squared times seven cubed.
<bookmark mark='fifth'/>The fifth has two twice and eigh twice.
It is two squared times eigh squared.

beats.on_screen: a × a × a × c × c × c × c × d: three a's, four c's, one d

marks.three: the repeats in the sixth are counted: three a's, four c's, one d
marks.once: the single d is circled and given no exponent

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, the sixth has eigh three times, see four times and dee once.
<bookmark mark='once'/>A letter that appears once needs no small number.

beats.on_screen: Check: 4; 2; 4; 2 + 3 = 5; 2 + 2 = 4; 3 + 4 + 1 = 8, each equal to the factors on the board

marks.check: the factor counts 4, 2 and 4 are matched to the first three
marks.sums: 2 + 3 = 5, 2 + 2 = 4 and 3 + 4 + 1 = 8 are matched to the last three

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check the counts against the factors on the board.
Four, two and four match the first three.
<bookmark mark='sums'/>Two and three make five, and two and two make four.
Three, four and one make eight, which matches the sixth.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>The last one is eigh cubed, see to the power four, dee.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>The first three are six to the power four, why squared and bee to the power four.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>The next two are five squared times seven cubed, and two squared times eigh squared.
